sections.content: How many people are "large goods vehicle drivers"?

242,050 people

were counted on the census as "large goods vehicle drivers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
LGV drivers collect, transport and deliver goods in rigid vehicles over 7 tonnes, articulated lorries and lorries pulling trailers.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "large goods vehicle drivers" there were more men than women (98.1% compared with 1.9%).

This means "large goods vehicle drivers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 98.1% and women made up 1.9% of "large goods vehicle drivers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "large goods vehicle drivers" included:

  • floorers and wall tilers
  • mobile machine drivers and operatives (other)
  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "large goods vehicle drivers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "large goods vehicle drivers", 17.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "large goods vehicle drivers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "large goods vehicle drivers" included:

  • podiatrists
  • inspectors of standards and regulations
  • property, housing and estate managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "large goods vehicle drivers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "large goods vehicle drivers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "large goods vehicle drivers", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.5% compared with 5.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.6%) than self-employed (10.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included North Northamptonshire, this is in the region of the East Midlands.
